newsitem.title: MALAWI: Malawi plans to double its communications capacity.
newsitem.headline: Malawi plans to double its communications capacity.

text.p: Malawi plans to spend more than $70 million over the next three years to more than double its telephone capacity, the country's communications chief said on Friday.
"Our capacity will jump from 40,000 to 95,000 lines to benefit our economy," Posts and Telecommunications Corporation (MPTC) Chief Executive, Steve Mijiga, told Reuters.
He said a project had been launched 18 months ago to replace the country's old system with digital and electronic exchanges.
The project is being financed by the African Development Bank with a $36 million loan.
Japan's Mitsui company helped to install 5,000 lines to people living in Malawi's second city of Blantyre at a cost of $10 million.
Bidders are currently being considered for the installation of telephone cables for other cities.
Mijiga said this phase was critical as MPTC was unable to connect most of the customers due to a lack of cables.
"The provision of this component will be very critical for the expansion of our services. It also happens to be the most complex of the project," he said.
Part of this phase has been awarded to France's Alacatel at a cost of $1,575,278 to supply 16,000 telephones, 1,100 secretarial sets and 517 private automatic branch exchanges (PABX).
"When this component is completed we'll be providing something like 43,000 telephones," Mijiga said.

In June, MPTC expects to sign an agreement with the Kuwait Fund for a $10 million off-shore loan, while a further $4 million is to be sourced locally to provide 10,000 lines in the districts of Thyolo, Mulanje, Phalombe Nsanje and Chikwawa.
